Rohan / Dana —

I reviewed the redlines. Thank you for the clear ask. Summary of our proposed approach below — goal is to minimize open-ended publicity exposure while preserving both parties' ability to reference the relationship for non-confidential, marketing purposes.

1) Confidentiality carveout: We cannot accept a blanket exception that displaces confidentiality obligations. Instead we propose a narrow exceptions clause: vendor may use customer name/logo for identification in marketing materials provided: (a) a draft is submitted for Customer's review, (b) Customer has 7 business days to object, and (c) no Confidential Information (as defined in the MSA) is disclosed in the public statement.

2) Reference rights: We will accept a limited reference right for non-sensitive product descriptions limited to high-level use cases. All case studies or press releases require written approval. We can add a 10 business day review window for approvals; we would ask for reciprocity for Redwood-initiated announcements.

3) Embargo: We can agree to an embargo clause but want to cap it at 21 calendar days in rare cases; standard is 10 business days as Rohan suggested. If Celerate requires longer for strategic pre-briefs, we can accept 30 days with mutual written agreement per announcement.

4) Logo usage: We require use of the official brand assets and a link to the brand guide plus a short approved usage statement. We will add a cross-reference in the Order Form to the brand_guidelines link.

Proposed next step: I will send a tracked-change Order Form with the updated clauses and a short summary ballot for signature. Dana, can you confirm Celerate's acceptance of the 7-day objection window (for identification use) and the 10 business day standard review for press/case studies?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
